questions.question: Describe the contribution of Buddhism to Shramanic thought. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Buddhism enriched Shramanic thought - rejected Vedic ritualism and questioned
  • Brahmanical authority-emphasised the Four Noble Truths - the Eightfold Path - non-violence,
  • compassion, and ethical conduct -its teachings challenged social inequalities and presented
  • liberation as achievable through wisdom, discipline, and personal effort rather than ritual
  • sacrifices.

questions.question: Explain Ambedkar’s argument that the caste system is a "division of labourers" rather than simply a benign "division of labour." / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar described caste as a “division of labourers” rather than merely a division of
  • labour- because it hierarchically organises people by birth - caste system imposes hereditary
  • occupations- restricts occupational mobility- perpetuates graded inequality- unlike functional
  • specialisation, caste denies individual freedom, dignity, fraternity and equal opportunities.

  • untouchability- social exclusion- advocates equality, dignity, representation, social justice, and
  • redistribution of power- drawing on thinkers such as Phule, Ambedkar, and Periyar, it promotes
  • education, constitutional rights, collective mobilisation, and the emancipation of oppressed
  • communities.
